t: The Secretary of the Air Force may not retire any F–117 Nighthawk attack aircraft during fiscal year 2006.

fable.w: This provision only bars a federal official from retiring certain aircraft during a fiscal year. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The only actor is the Secretary of the Air Force, who is inside the federal government.
fable.s: The Secretary of the Air Force may not retire any F–117 Nighthawk attack aircraft during fiscal year 2006.

qwen_block.w: This section imposes a restriction on a federal official (the Secretary of the Air Force) regarding the retirement of military aircraft. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government, such as the public, states, or private entities. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of the Air Force may not retire any F–117 Nighthawk attack aircraft during fiscal year 2006.

opus.w: This section only stops a federal official (the Secretary of the Air Force) from retiring certain aircraft during one fiscal year. It brings in no state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public through consultation, a hearing, a comment period, an advisory body, rulemaking or a right to sue. Limiting a federal decision is not the same as having outsiders take part in it.
opus.s: The Secretary of the Air Force may not retire any F–117 Nighthawk attack aircraft during fiscal year 2006.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a restriction on a federal official (the Secretary of the Air Force) regarding the retirement of military aircraft. It does not require or recommend consultation, coordination, or participation with any entity outside the federal government. The decision is made internally within the executive branch.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of the Air Force may not retire any F–117 Nighthawk attack aircraft during fiscal year 2006.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the prohibition on retiring aircraft implies a consultation with pilots or maintenance crews, but the text contains no such requirement. The section is a direct command to a federal official regarding asset management. It does not involve any outside party (state, local, public, private) in the decision-making process.
